newsitem.title: FRANCE: France launches probe into anti-Pope pastry gang.
newsitem.headline: France launches probe into anti-Pope pastry gang.

text.p: A French prosecutor opened a probe on Monday into a gang of cream-cake throwers who attacked priests in a cathedral to protest at a planned visit to France by Pope John Paul.

The preliminary investigation by the Nantes prosecutor's office in north-west France, into "pre-meditated violence and hindering freedom of expression", was partly aimed at deterring further pastry salvoes, judicial sources said.

About 20 protestors hurled cream cakes and water-filled condoms during the service in Nantes cathedral on Sunday, forcing one of the priests to the ground. Two people were arrested but later released.

The probe will seek to identify the protesters, who were led by Georges Le Gloupier, a Belgian self-styled anarchist whose trademark is throwing cream cakes at personalities in public places like the Cannes film festival.

In a statement to the Belgian news agency Belga, Le Gloupier said the Nantes "pastry hurricane" was the first in a series of attacks he planned with French allies unless the Pope cancelled his September 19-22 visit.
"Popes, bishops and priestlings -- let's cover them with icing," he said.

The Pope's visit is triggering unprecedented opposition in France, where about 80 percent of the population call themselves Roman Catholics, largely because of papal opposition to birth control, abortion and homosexuality.
A crude bomb was defused early this month in a church where the Pontiff is due to pray on the first day of his visit.
